doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

chapter: Joining and playing in the Basie band
title: Why Basie never let him play ballads
summary: Featured on uptempo pieces, Foster asked for a ballad; Basie refused, and Foster agrees his tone was not ready, citing 'Ain't Misbehavin''.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. Did Basie ever indicate dissatisfaction with your playing? What you were feeling yourself, did you feel that from him?

No, he didn’t, only on one occasion he made me feel that way. I was featured on several uptempo pieces, like “Little Pony,” “Jumpin’ at the Woodside,” and that sort of became my specialty. And one time I approached him and I said, “Bas’, why don’t you let me play a ballad?” And he said, “well you do all right on ‘Jumpin’ at the Woodside,’ you don’t need to play a ballad.” And he said this because he knew that I could not play a ballad at the time. I just — a ballad played with a bebop concept didn’t fit that band. Don Byas, Lester Young, Coleman Hawkins, Herschel Evans, those guys played ballads in a

manner that would fit the Basie band. But I wanted to be all over my horn. I didn’t want to settle down on a simple melody. And I got a chance to play all I knew on the songs, like “Jumpin’ at the Woodside,” the uptempo songs. But he was right. My tone had not developed to a logical point where I was a good choice for a ballad. And it was proven on record. There is a recording that I hope you won’t go listen to.
Let me see if I have it here—

Of me playing “Ain’t Misbehavin’” with the Basie orchestra. And I tried to emulate Sonny Stitt playing it. He had a version of “Ain’t Misbehavin.’” But I listened to it later and I said no this is not happening. I just wasn’t — I didn’t have the sound or the approach to play a ballad convincingly with the Basie orchestra. And he saw to it that I didn’t play any ballads, and rightly so.

He knew what he wanted. It’s interesting you mentioned tone, because the tone issue shows up so much more when you’re playing a ballad. As you mentioned, if you’re playing an uptempo thing, maybe your tone, it goes by so quick—
Right. You can get away with not having a well rounded, full big sound.

Now I have made comparisons with myself, my present, the 1980s, 1990s Frank Foster and the 1950s Frank Foster, and I think Basie would like the way I play a ballad now. If I could have played a ballad then the way I can play one now, I think he would have accepted me.
Was it just the years of experience?
Hello. That’s all it was. And developing a sound along with the years of experience.
